idea-plugin.name: Laravel Warrant
idea-plugin.description:
Syntax highlighting for the Warrant authorization rule language. Highlights standalone .warrant files and, more importantly, the DSL embedded in PHP: heredocs/nowdocs labelled WARRANT, and strings wherever rule text is expected, such as warrant('...') and Warrant::parse('...').

Starts the Warrant language server that ships with the patrickhanna/laravel-warrant Composer package, for errors, hover, completion, go-to-definition and quick fixes in .warrant files and in the Warrant inside PHP files. The server is found at vendor/bin/warrant-language-server and run with PHP; configure it under Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Warrant. Language-server support needs a PhpStorm version that ships the IntelliJ Platform LSP API (2024.2 or later).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.7.1 — Make the plugin's icon an inked rubber stamp: WARRANT across a round stamp, with “for Laravel” around its foot. The .warrant file icon stays as it is.
  • 0.7.0 — Close (, {, ' and " as they are typed, highlight the matching bracket at the caret, indent the line Enter opens inside a { } block, and comment lines out with #, in .warrant files and in Warrant inside PHP. Colour the escapes in a string, \', \" and \\, and mark any other backslash pair as an invalid escape. An unclosed string is coloured to the end of its line only, as the language reads it, rather than to the end of the text. Give .warrant files an icon, and the plugin a logo to match: a rubber stamp's ring with a W.
  • 0.6.1 — Underline a name in Warrant text on Cmd/Ctrl-hover when the language server knows where it is declared, and go there on click.
  • 0.6.0 — Start the Warrant language server for .warrant and PHP files: diagnostics, hover, completion, go-to-definition and quick fixes. Adds Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Warrant (enable, PHP executable, server path, vocabulary) and Tools | Restart Warrant Language Server.
  • 0.5.0 — Highlight Warrant inside PHP wherever rule text is expected: the first argument of warrant(), Warrant::parse(), WarrantSyntax::parse(), WarrantParser::parse() and ->ifRaw() / ->orIfRaw(), and a string returned from rules() or a #[DerivedCondition] / #[RuleTemplate] method.
  • 0.2.0 — Highlight @sql "<sql>" raw SQL references alongside @context and @column.
  • 0.1.0 — Initial release: Warrant DSL syntax highlighting, including injection into PHP heredocs labelled WARRANT.
